newsitem.title: USA: U.S. light vehicle sales rose 1.9 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. light vehicle sales rose 1.9 percent in 1996.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales for the full 1996 year totaled 15.14 million units, an increase of 1.9 percent over the 14.76 million sold in 1995, according to figures released by major automakers.
All carmakers have reported year-end U.S. results except for German sports car maker Porsche AG. The year-to-date totals include Porsche sales through November.
The year-to-year percentage change is based on a daily sales rate derived from 308 selling days in 1996 versus 306 days in 1995.
The industry's U.S. sales performance in 1996 matched the 15.1 million light vehicles sold in the United States during 1994, which had been the highest since 1988.
During the month of December, U.S. light vehicle sales totaled 1,126,558 vehicles, excluding Porsche results. The total was 4.0 percent below the 1,173,937 vehicles sold in December 1995.
The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 14.5 million units, down from 15.9 million units a year earlier and 14.9 million for the month of November 1996.
The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
Automakers sold 499,122 North American-built cars in the United States in December, down 8.3 percent from a year ago.
Automakers sold 483,289 domestic trucks in the United States during December, down 0.5 percent from a year earlier.
General Motors Corp's sales for the month fell 14.2 percent, while its sales for the full year fell 2.7 percent to a total of 4.74 million cars and light trucks.
Ford Motor Co. reported that its sales for the month rose 10.6 percent, while its total for the full year rose a scant 0.5 percent to 3.84 million.
Chrysler Corp reported a 1.1 percent increase in sales for December, while its full-year total rose 12.4 percent to 2.45 million units.
